title: Status polling can continually abort slow metrics requests
test: tests/metricsFetcher.test.js: 'poll ticks during a request slower than the poll interval do not cancel it', 'a load while one is in flight returns that same request and aborts nothing', 'a request that exceeds the timeout fails visibly and is aborted with a timeout reason', 'the timeout also covers a response whose body never arrives', 'a timeout settles the request even when the fetch ignores the abort signal', 'aborting for unmount cancels the request silently', 'an explicit retry replaces a stuck request silently and starts a fresh one', 'an abort the fetcher did not cause is reported, not swallowed', 'applyMetricsResult keeps the last metrics and shows the error when a refresh times out', 'StatusView polls through the single-flight fetcher and only aborts at unmount'
proof: Holds. StatusView.fetchMetrics began with abortRef.current?.abort() and the poller called it every 5000 ms (and on becoming visible), so a metrics request slower than the interval was cancelled by the next tick; the AbortError was swallowed (if (err?.name === 'AbortError') return;), no timeout existed, and nothing was ever shown. The fetch logic lived inside the component, so it could not be run on its own: the new tests were written against a small extracted loader (src/lib/metricsFetcher.mjs, createMetricsFetcher({ fetchImpl, timeoutMs, timers })) and first run against a stand-in that carries the old StatusView logic behind that interface (abort the previous request on every call, swallow AbortError, no timeout). Of 20 tests 10 failed on it: the poll-tick test with 'the 5s tick must not abort the slow request: true !== false' (the 5 s tick aborted the in-flight request, which the old code did), the overlap test ('overlapping callers must share the in-flight promise'), and the timeout tests ('the request never settled': a request exceeding 15 s just hangs, with no error), plus the retry/abort-cause tests and the StatusView source guard (the view still held its own AbortController and abort-per-call). Fix: createMetricsFetcher returns the outstanding promise when load() is called again, gives each request its own AbortController and a 15 s timeout (DEFAULT_METRICS_TIMEOUT_MS, section-49e0545c60d121dd3e784d86/Q-004), and tracks why it aborted: a timeout settles as { status: 'error', message: 'Metrics request timed out.' } and surfaces through the existing 'Refresh failed' alert (or the Unavailable card before any metrics loaded) while the last metrics stay on screen; only an unmount abort (and a Retry replacing a stuck request) settles as 'aborted' and is ignored; any other abort is shown as an error. A race against the abort signal settles a request even if fetch ignores the signal, so a hung request cannot hold single-flight open. StatusView folds each result through applyMetricsResult in a useReducer; 401/403 still map to the Access restricted card; unmount calls fetcher.abort(). All 22 tests of the file pass after the fix. A real-browser run of the built page against server.js with a slow or never-answered /api/metrics confirmed it: an 8 s response rendered after a 5 s tick with one request and none cancelled; a request that hung after a first success showed 'Refresh failed: Metrics request timed out.' after 15 s with the metrics still on screen and the 5 s/10 s ticks joining it (2 requests total); with nothing ever answering the Unavailable card showed the timeout and Retry started a fresh request and recovered; a 403 still showed Access restricted.
